# slideimp

[slideimp](https://github.com/hhp94/slideimp) is a lightweight R package
for fast K-NN and PCA imputation of missing values in high-dimensional
numeric matrices (samples in rows, variables in columns). Its main
functions:

- [`group_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/group_imp.md):
  group-wise K-NN or PCA imputation, wrapping
  [`knn_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/knn_imp.md)
  and
  [`pca_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/pca_imp.md)
  (e.g., by chromosome for Illumina DNAm microarrays such as 450K, EPIC,
  EPICv2, MSA).

- [`slide_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/slide_imp.md):
  sliding window K-NN or PCA imputation over columns ordered by
  position, wrapping
  [`knn_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/knn_imp.md)
  and
  [`pca_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/pca_imp.md).
  **Note**: not intended for Illumina microarrays, use
  [`group_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/group_imp.md)
  instead.

- [`pca_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/pca_imp.md):
  optimized reimplementation of
  [`missMDA::imputePCA()`](http://factominer.free.fr/missMDA/PCA.md) for
  high-dimensional matrices. Supports a LOBPCG eigensolver that
  warm-starts each EM iteration from the previous eigenblock and search
  direction.

- [`knn_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/knn_imp.md):
  full K-NN imputation with
  [RcppThread](https://github.com/tnagler/RcppThread) multi-threading.
  Supports `subset` imputation to restrict work to specific columns
  (e.g., clock CpGs) for very fast targeted imputation.

- [`mipca()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/mipca.md):
  Bayesian PCA sampler that draws multiple imputations of the missing
  values, with the method of [Audigier, Husson and Josse
  (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1080/00949655.2015.1104683). Recommended
  for whole-genome methylation data (WGBS, EM-seq), which are sparsely
  observed. See the [multiple imputation
  article](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/articles/multiple-imputation-beta.html).

- [`mipca_flank()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/mipca_flank.md):
  runs [`mipca()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/mipca.md)
  on target CpGs.

## Installation

The stable version of [slideimp](https://github.com/hhp94/slideimp) can
be installed from CRAN using:

``` r

install.packages("slideimp")
```

You can install the development version of
[slideimp](https://github.com/hhp94/slideimp) with:

``` r

pak::pkg_install("hhp94/slideimp")
```

You can install the optional
[`slideimp.extra`](https://github.com/hhp94/slideimp.extra) package
(which provides lightweight Illumina manifests) with:

``` r

pak::pkg_install("hhp94/slideimp.extra")
```

## Citation

To cite [slideimp](https://github.com/hhp94/slideimp), use the
Bioinformatics paper:

``` bibtex
@article{10.1093/bioinformatics/btag318,
    author = {Pham, Hung and Lombroso, Adam P and Cevik, Esma Cansu and Taylor, Hugh S and O'Donnell, Kieran J},
    title = {slideimp: efficient imputation of {DNA} methylation data},
    journal = {Bioinformatics},
    volume = {42},
    number = {6},
    pages = {btag318},
    year = {2026},
    doi = {10.1093/bioinformatics/btag318},
    month = jun,
}
```

## PCA or K-NN imputation of Illumina DNAm microarrays

- This is a simulated beta matrix from the
  [MSA](https://www.illumina.com/products/by-type/microarray-kits/infinium-methylation-screening-array.html)
  microarray. CpGs are in columns.

``` r

dim(MSA_beta_matrix)
#> [1]     20 281797
MSA_beta_matrix[1:4, 1:4]
#>         cg06185909_TC11 cg18975462_BC11 cg20516119_TC11 cg10149399_BC11
#> sample1              NA       0.5023435       0.3835431              NA
#> sample2       0.4907466       0.5095459       0.9025816       0.4313347
#> sample3       0.6885036              NA       0.7646753       0.4498772
#> sample4       0.0000000       0.0000000              NA       0.0000000
```

- Chromosome-wise imputation of Illumina microarrays can be performed
  with a single function call (requires the Illumina manifests, which
  the [`slideimp.extra`](https://github.com/hhp94/slideimp.extra)
  package provides).

- This example demonstrates PCA imputation. To use K-NN imputation
  instead, supply the `k` argument.

``` r

library(slideimp.extra)
library(slideimp)

imputed <- group_imp(
  obj = MSA_beta_matrix,
  group = "MSA", # <- this feature requires the `slideimp.extra` package
  ncp = 10, # <- change to `k` for K-NN imputation. Optimal value requires `tune_imp()`.
  clamp = c(0, 1), # <- PCA imputation can generate values outside of `c(0, 1)`
  .progress = FALSE # <- turn on to monitor progress of longer running jobs
)
#> Found cleaned manifest for 'MSA'
#> ! 1 group dropped: no feature matches a column name.
#> ℹ Dropped group: M
#> Imputing 25 groups using PCA.
#> Running mode: sequential

print(imputed, n = 4, p = 4)
#> Method: group_imp (PCA imputation)
#> Dimensions: 20 x 281797
#> 
#>         cg06185909_TC11 cg18975462_BC11 cg20516119_TC11 cg10149399_BC11
#> sample1       0.1517542       0.5023435      0.38354308       0.2067731
#> sample2       0.4907466       0.5095459      0.90258164       0.4313347
#> sample3       0.6885036       0.7339375      0.76467530       0.4498772
#> sample4       0.0000000       0.0000000      0.05230101       0.0000000
#> # Showing 4 of 20 rows and 4 of 281797 columns
```

### Troubleshooting tips

- [`group_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/group_imp.md)
  fails with unmapped probes: your matrix likely contains
  [`sesame`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/sesame.html)-generated
  control probes (prefixed `ctl_`) or you picked the wrong manifest
  (`"EPICv2"` vs. `"EPICv2_deduped"`). Check the manifest, remove
  `"ctl"` probes with `obj <- obj[, !grepl("^ctl", colnames(obj))]`, or
  pass `allow_unmapped = TRUE` to bypass.
- Impute the MSA or EPICv2 data **with** the duplicated probes, then
  dedup with `slideimp.extra::dedup_matrix()`.

### Performance tips

- For tips on the `solver` choice and LOBPCG warm-start, plus
  `threshold`, `scale`, and [mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org)/BLAS
  threading, see [Speeding up PCA
  imputation](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/articles/speeding-up-pca-imputation.html).
- For PCA imputation of bounded data, i.e., DNA methylation beta values,
  use `clamp = c(0, 1)` to restrict PCA-imputed values to the valid
  range.
- For parallel PCA imputation,
  [`group_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/group_imp.md)
  and
  [`tune_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/tune_imp.md)
  pin BLAS to one thread on each [mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org)
  worker, so BLAS threads and workers do not compete for cores. Set
  `pin_blas = FALSE` to turn this off. On Windows with OpenBLAS, the pin
  does not reach every call. See [Speeding up PCA
  imputation](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/articles/speeding-up-pca-imputation.html)
  for the fix.
- For faster PCA imputation on Windows machines, advanced users can
  replace R’s default reference BLAS with OpenBLAS. See [this community
  guide](https://github.com/david-cortes/R-openblas-in-windows).
- For parallel K-NN imputation, use the `cores` argument, which uses
  [RcppThread](https://github.com/tnagler/RcppThread)’s `parallelFor`,
  instead of [mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org). If you only need clock
  CpGs, pass `subset` to skip all other probes.

## Extended Workflow

- Simulate DNA methylation (DNAm) microarray data from 2 chromosomes.
  All [slideimp](https://github.com/hhp94/slideimp) functions expect the
  input to be a double matrix (convert an integer matrix with
  `storage.mode(obj) <- "double"`) where variables are stored in the
  columns.

``` r

library(slideimp)
set.seed(1234)
sim_obj <- sim_mat(n = 20, p = 100, n_col_groups = 2)

# `input` holds the simulated matrix with missing data
obj <- sim_obj$input

# `col_group` holds the column-wise grouping
group_df <- sim_obj$col_group
```

- Tune the hyperparameters with
  [`tune_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/tune_imp.md).
  This grid search evaluates these K-NN imputation options:

  - Number of nearest neighbors (`k`): 5 or 20
  - Inverse distance power (`dist_pow`) for weighted averaging: 1 or 2
    (higher values assign lower weights to more distant neighbors)

- The tuning runs on a subset of the data. It uses 10 repeats of
  cross-validation (`n_reps = 10`). Each repeat masks 50 observed values
  (`num_na = 50`) and computes the RMSE and MAE. Use larger values for
  both `n_reps` and `num_na` in real analyses for more reliable error
  estimates.

``` r

knn_params <- expand.grid(k = c(5, 20), dist_pow = c(1, 2))
group2_columns <- subset(group_df, group == "group2")
group2_only <- obj[, group2_columns$feature]

tune_knn <- tune_imp(
  group2_only,
  parameters = knn_params,
  .f = "knn_imp",
  cores = 8, # <- only available for K-NN imputation
  n_reps = 10,
  num_na = 50
)
#> Tuning `knn_imp()`
#> Step 1/2: Resolving NA locations
#> Running mode: threaded (8 cores)
#> Step 2/2: Tuning
```

- Calculate errors using
  [`compute_metrics()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/compute_metrics.md)
  or [yardstick](https://github.com/tidymodels/yardstick) functions.

``` r

metrics <- compute_metrics(tune_knn)
aggregate(.estimate ~ k + dist_pow + .metric, data = metrics, FUN = mean)
#>    k dist_pow .metric .estimate
#> 1  5        1     mae 0.1636596
#> 2 20        1     mae 0.1473074
#> 3  5        2     mae 0.1654782
#> 4 20        2     mae 0.1487407
#> 5  5        1    rmse 0.2098225
#> 6 20        1    rmse 0.1898989
#> 7  5        2    rmse 0.2120673
#> 8 20        2    rmse 0.1926341
```

- For PCA imputation and custom functions, set up parallelization with
  [`mirai::daemons()`](https://mirai.r-lib.org/reference/daemons.html).
  See [Speeding up PCA
  imputation](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/articles/speeding-up-pca-imputation.html)
  for more guidance on PCA performance.

``` r

mirai::daemons(2) # 2 Cores

# PCA imputation.
pca_params <- data.frame(ncp = c(1, 5))
tune_pca <- tune_imp(obj, parameters = pca_params, .f = "pca_imp", n_reps = 10, num_na = 50)

mirai::daemons(0) # Close daemons
```

- Then perform imputation with
  [`group_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/group_imp.md)
  using the best parameters.

``` r

knn_group_results <- group_imp(obj, group = group_df, k = 20, dist_pow = 1, cores = 2)
#> Imputing 2 groups using K-NN.
#> Running mode: threaded (2 cores)
knn_group_results
#> Method: group_imp (K-NN imputation)
#> Dimensions: 20 x 100
#> 
#>          feature1  feature2  feature3  feature4  feature5  feature6
#> sample1 0.3486482 0.7385414 0.4077444 0.1607935 0.3924661 0.2434143
#> sample2 0.5338935 0.4724364 0.9663621 0.4788070 0.5061132 0.3923603
#> sample3 0.7185848 0.7351035 0.6724479 0.3162537 0.7634236 1.0000000
#> sample4 0.1734418 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.2106358
#> sample5 0.5388440 0.5306182 0.5685354 0.5383513 0.4680080 0.8518388
#> sample6 0.3768380 0.5570723 0.8764909 0.5276245 0.6722794 0.5740639
#> # Showing 6 of 20 rows and 6 of 100 columns
```

- [`group_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/group_imp.md)
  runs PCA imputation in parallel on [mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org)
  daemons in the same way as
  [`tune_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/tune_imp.md).

- Alternatively, full matrix imputation can be performed using
  [`knn_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/knn_imp.md)
  or
  [`pca_imp()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/pca_imp.md).

``` r

full_knn_results <- knn_imp(obj = obj, k = 20)
full_pca_results <- pca_imp(obj = obj, ncp = 10)
```

## Multiple imputation of WGBS/EM-seq data

- For WGBS/EM-seq data,
  [`mipca_flank()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/mipca_flank.md)
  draws multiple imputations of target CpGs, each fitted on the CpGs
  within `window_size` bp of it. Split the data by chromosome first.
- This simulated beta matrix stands in for one chromosome, with 50 to
  500 bp between neighboring CpGs.

``` r

set.seed(1234)
chr1_beta <- sim_mat(n = 30, p = 500, beta = TRUE)$input
location <- cumsum(sample(50:500, ncol(chr1_beta), replace = TRUE))
```

- First, find the window of each target with
  [`mipca_flank_plan()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/mipca_flank.md).

``` r

targets <- colnames(chr1_beta)[c(100, 250, 400)]
plan <- mipca_flank_plan(
  chr1_beta,
  location,
  window_size = 2000, # bp on each side of the target
  subset = targets,
  min_window_n = 10
)
plan
#> si_flank_plan: 3 targets on a 30 x 500 matrix, nothing fitted
#>   status: impute 2, clean 1
#>  target       name n_miss start end window_n status
#>     100 feature100      6    94 105       12 impute
#>     250 feature250      0   244 256       13  clean
#>     400 feature400      6   393 406       14 impute
#>   next: mipca_flank(x, rank, seed, transform) imputes.
#>         mipca_flank_window(x, subset) gives one target's window to tune on.
```

- Then fit each window and keep the targets’ draws. Choose `rank` with
  [`mipca_tune()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/mipca_tune.md)
  on one target’s window.

``` r

fit <- mipca_flank(plan, rank = 2, seed = 1, transform = "logit_biwhiten", .progress = FALSE)
fit
#> si_mi fit: 30 x 3, 12 imputed cells, 400 draws
#>   next: as.matrix() with 'draw' for a completed matrix, summary() for Rhat and ESS
```

- See the [multiple imputation
  article](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/articles/multiple-imputation-beta.html)
  for tuning, convergence checks, and pooling the draws.

## Other functions

- [`col_vars()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/col_vars.md):
  Column-wise variance, skipping missing values.
- [`mat_miss()`](https://hhp94.github.io/slideimp/reference/mat_miss.md):
  Efficient column or row missing statistics.
